title: Training-Free Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models via Persona Disagreement
abstract: arXiv:2605.10843v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models now take part in decisions that rest on moral preferences, and those preferences differ by country. A model's default preferences sit closest to one population, so a single deployment serves every country with one country's values. Existing fixes need per-culture training data, a per-country reward model, or access to model internals, which the countries furthest from that default rarely have. We show how far a country can be reached without any of them. Our method, DISCA, keeps the model's weights frozen, sees no country-specific human targets, and reads only the model's score for each answer option. It builds a country as a panel of four persona prompts grounded in World Values Survey microdata. translated_title: 通过角色分歧实现大语言模型的无训练文化对齐
translated_abstract: 大语言模型如今参与到依赖于道德偏好的决策中，而这些偏好因国家而异。模型的默认偏好最接近某一个人群，因此单一的部署会用一个国家的价值观来服务所有国家。现有的解决方案需要针对每种文化的训练数据、针对每个国家的奖励模型，或访问模型内部结构——而距离该默认值最远的国家往往缺乏这些资源。我们展示了在完全没有这些资源的情况下，能够将模型适配到多远的国家。我们的方法DISCA保持模型权重冻结，不使用任何国家特定的人类标注目标，只读取模型对每个答案选项的评分。该方法基于世界价值观调查的微观数据，将一个国家构建为由四个角色提示组成的评审面板。面板的共识设定一个以国家为条件的锚点，超出该锚点的损失规避式精细化调整只有在两次独立运行结果一致时才被保留，同时一个持续更新的国家级先验会汇集已做出的决策……
tldr: 提出DISCA方法，无需训练、无需特定国家的数据或访问模型内部，仅通过基于世界价值观调查数据构建的四角色提示面板的共识与分歧机制，即可将权重冻结的大语言模型对齐到不同国家的道德偏好。
en_tdlr: DISCA enables training-free cultural alignment of frozen-weight LLMs to country-specific moral preferences by building a four-persona panel from World Values Survey microdata, using panel consensus as an anchor and keeping refinements only when two independent runs agree.
